questions.question: Which of the following is the key aspect of Constitutional bodies?

options.text: Made by the President and PM

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mentioned in the Constitution**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Constitutional bodies are institutions that derive their powers and authority from the provisions explicitly stated in the Constitution of India. 
 
• These bodies cannot be altered or removed without amending the Constitution itself. 
 
• Examples include the Election Commission of India, the Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG), and the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)
 
• 
 
Mentioned in the Constitution:

 
 
• 
 
These bodies are specifically referred to in various articles of the Indian Constitution. For example:

 
 
• Election Commission of India: Article 324
 
• Union Public Service Commission (UPSC): Articles 315-323
 
• Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG): Article 148
 
• Finance Commission: Article 280
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
Made by the Parliament:

 
This refers to statutory bodies, which are established by laws passed in Parliament. Examples include the National Green Tribunal (NGT) or the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC). These are not mentioned in the Constitution.

 
 
• 
 
Made by the President and PM:

 
The President and Prime Minister alone do not have the power to create constitutional bodies. The creation of such bodies requires constitutional provisions.

 
 
• 
 
Temporary Status:

 
Constitutional bodies are permanent and exist as long as the Constitution itself. Temporary bodies, such as a commission set up for a specific purpose, are different and are not constitutional bodies.

questions.question: What is the name of the phenomenon by which light splits into its component colours upon passing through a prism?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dispersion**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** phenomenon where white light splits into its component colors when passing through a prism is called dispersion. **
 
• White light is made up of **seven bands of colors**, each with a different wavelength. 
 
• When white light passes through a medium, each color travels at a different speed and has a different angle of refraction. 
 
• **This causes the light to split, or disperse. **
 
• **For example**, when light travels from air into water, it slows down, causing it to continue to travel at a different angle or direction. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Diffraction**

 
 
• When a **wave passes through a small opening or around a barrier, it bends and spreads out.**
 
• This can be demonstrated by placing obstacles in a ripple tank and observing the path of the water waves. 
 
 
 
• **Reflection**
 
 
• When **light rays bounce off a surface**.
 
• The law of reflection states that the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence. 
 
 
 
• **Refraction**
 
 
• When a **ray of light passes from one medium to another, it changes direction at the boundary.**
 
• The path of the light depends on the density of the materials.
 
• **For example, l**ight bends toward the normal when it travels from a less dense medium to a denser medium. 
 
 
 
• **Rainbows are formed by a combination of refraction, dispersion, and total internal reflection.**
 
• When **sunlight passes through water droplets in the atmosphere, the droplets act like prisms, refracting and dispersing the light, reflecting it internally, and then refracting it again when it exits the droplet**.

questions.question:
Which of the given statements about Phylum Angiosperms are correct?

A. Angiosperms are non-vascular plants with stems, roots and leaves.

B. The seeds of the angiosperm are naked.

C. These make up the majority of all plants on earth.

D. The seeds develop inside the plant organs and form fruit.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only C and D**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **These make up the majority of all plants on Earth**.

 
 
• **Angiosperms**, or flowering plants,** represent the largest and most diverse group of plants in the plant kingdom.**
 
• They** account for about 80-90% **of all known plant species, which means the majority of plants we encounter daily, such as trees, shrubs, grasses, and herbs, belong to this group.
 
• **Angiosperms thrive in a wide variety of habitats**, from forests and grasslands to deserts and aquatic environments.
 
• Their dominance is due to several evolutionary advantages, including:
 
 
• Efficient vascular system (xylem and phloem) for water and nutrient transport.
 
• The development of flowers that attract pollinators (like bees, birds, and bats), increasing their chances of reproduction.
 
• The production of fruits that help in the protection and dispersal of seeds by animals, wind, or water.
 
 
 
• **Examples of angiosperms** include mango trees, wheat, roses, and grass species.
 
• Hence **this statement is correct**
 
 
 
• **The seeds develop inside the plant organs and form fruit**.
 
 
• In **angiosperms, seeds are enclosed within a protective structure known as the ovary.**
 
• This **feature distinguishes them from gymnosperms, where seeds are exposed ("naked seeds").**
 
• Here’s the process:
 
 
• **Reproduction in Angiosperms:** Angiosperms reproduce sexually via flowers. After pollination and fertilization, the ovules within the ovary develop into seeds.
 
• **Formation of Fruit: **The ovary surrounding the seeds matures into a fruit, which serves two critical functions:
 
• **Protection of Seeds: **The fruit safeguards the seeds during their development.
 
• **Seed Dispersal: **Fruits aid in dispersal, as they may be eaten by animals, carried by wind, or float on water to spread seeds to new locations.
 
 
 
• **For example:**
 
• **In mangoes, the fleshy part we eat is the fruit, and the seed is enclosed inside it.**
 
• **In peas, the pod is the fruit, and the seeds are the peas inside the pod.​**
 
• **Hence this statement is correct**

questions.question: In which of the following Articles of the Constitution of India is it mentioned that “it shall be the duty of every citizen of India to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so”?

__
 
• The **Article of the Constitution of India that states that it is the duty of every citizen to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so is Article 51A. **
 
• National service is a system of government service that can be compulsory or voluntary.
 
• **In India,** there is no compulsory recruitment, but the National Service Act of 1972 allows certain people to be called to perform national service.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties under Article 51A**
 
• **51A(i):**
 
 
• "To safeguard public property and to abjure violence."
 
• This fundamental duty emphasizes the importance of protecting public assets and refraining from violent actions.
 
 
 
• **51A(k):**
 
 
• "Who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or ward between the age of six and fourteen years."
 
• This was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, making it a duty for parents/guardians to ensure children receive education.
 
 
 
• **51A(j)**:
 
 
• "To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavour and achievement."
 
• This duty encourages citizens to aim for excellence, contributing to the nation's progress

questions.question: Which of the following fundamental duties is violated when a person purposefully spoils an ancient monument?

options.text: To preserve our rich heritage and composite culture.
To protect the unity and integrity of India.
To develop a scientific outlook and humanism.
To defend the country when the need arises.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To preserve our rich heritage and composite culture**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fundamental Duty (Article 51A of the Indian Constitution):

 
 
• One of the fundamental duties of Indian citizens is to "preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture" (under 51A(f)).
 
 
 
• Violated Duty: When a person purposefully spoils an ancient monument, they are violating this duty because such actions harm India’s cultural heritage, which is considered an important part of the nation’s composite culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• To protect the unity and integrity of India: This duty is about maintaining national unity and would not directly apply to spoiling monuments.
 
• To develop a scientific outlook and humanism: This is more related to promoting rational thinking and social responsibility, but not directly related to heritage preservation.
 
• To defend the country when the need arises: This duty pertains to national defense, not cultural heritage.

• Regulation of commercial and regional rural banks.
 
• Licensing and monitoring the performance of banks.

• Ensuring adequate credit flow to various sectors of the economy.

• They do not have the responsibility of promoting or developing the overall banking system in the country.
 
• Commercial Bank
 
• Commercial banks (e.g., SBI, HDFC, ICICI) primarily focus on accepting deposits, lending money, and providing various financial services.
 
• While they are crucial for economic development and customer banking needs, they operate under the regulations set by the central bank and do not oversee the banking system as a whole.

• They play a role in rural development but do not oversee or promote the entire banking system's stability or growth.

__
 
• Kathak dance

 
 
• ​One of the eight primary styles of Indian classical dance is kathak.
 
• It is an Uttar Pradesh classical dancing style. The storytellers or itinerant bards known as Kathakars in ancient northern India are often credited as the creators of Kathak.
 
• The Vedic Sanskrit words Katha, which means "story," and Kathakar, which means "the one who tells a story" or "to do with stories," are the roots of the word Kathak.
 
• Traveling Kathakars used dance, songs, and music to transmit tales from the great epics and ancient mythology. Kathak dancers use intricate footwork, flexible body movements, and, most importantly, expressive face expressions to convey a variety of stories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Kathakali**

 
 
• Kathakali is a classical dance form that originates from Kerala, a state in the southern part of India.
 
• It is distinguished by its vibrant costumes, elaborate makeup, and face masks that the performers wear.
 
• Kathakali translates to "Story-Play" and is known for its intricate storytelling, detailed gestures, and expressive eye movements.
 
• The dance form combines dance, music, drama, and literature into a composite art form, making it unique and complex.
 
• Themes of Kathakali are mostly taken from the Indian epics like Mahabharata, Ramayana, and other ancient scriptures.
 
• It is performed exclusively by men and involves rigorous physical training to master the art form.
 
• The music used in Kathakali is called Sopanam and is sung in the Malayalam language.
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi **
 
 
• One of the eight principal Indian classical dances is Kuchipudi.
 
• It comes from the Andhra Pradesh state of India, specifically the village of Kuchipudi.
 
• Kuchipudi was created as a way to worship Krishna, a Hindu deity.
 
• Siddhendra Yogi, a gifted poet and visionary who belonged to the Vaishnava sect and had the ability to give some of his visions solid form, created the Kuchipudi style of Yakshagaana in the 17th century.
 
• Kuchipudi is renowned for its dynamic storytelling, dramatic characterization, outstanding, rapid dancing, and expressive eye movements.
 
• Tandava (the regal, masculine) and Lasya (lyrical graceful and feminine energy) are combined in this dance.
 
• Other famous dance forms of Andhra Pradesh include - Vilasini Natyam, Andhra Natyam, Bhamakalpam, Veeranatyam, Dappu, Tappeta Gullu, Lambadi, Dhimsa, Kolattam, Butta Bommalu.
 
 
 
• **​Bharatnatyam**
 
 
• Bharatnatyam dance origin can be traced from back to *Sadir*-the solo dance of temple dancer or devadasis in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Bharatnatyam is also known as *Dashiattam*.
 
• Elements of Bharatnatyam:
 
 
• Alarippu-seeking blessing of god with simple dance steps in rhythm.
 
• Jatiswaram-Nritta component with devoid expression.
 
• Shabdam-dramatic element with expressed words.
 
• Varnam-combination of dance and emotion to express a story.
 
• Padam-mastery over abhinaya of a spiritual message by the artist.
 
• Jawali-Its performed at short love lyrics at a fast tempo.

• Hikat is danced by forming pairs, extending their arms and with the body inclined, they go round and round at the same position.
 
• This dance is filled with joy and is associated with Jammu and Kashmir. 
 
• This dance is performed by everyone to welcome the spring season in Kashmir and celebrates the harvesting season.
 
• When the dance originated, there were no instruments or music, people hold their wrists and just sing and spin. As the dance progress, it speeds up and beats become faster.
 
 
• But nowadays, you will hear and feel the music and the sound of Rabab, drums accompanying the folk dance.
 
 
 
• Damali, Rauf and Mandjas are the other folk dances from Jammu and Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Rauf**
 
 
• Rauf is a traditional folk dance of Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It is performed mainly by women during the spring season and on various festive occasions.
 
• The dance is characterized by its rhythmic movements and is often accompanied by folk songs.
 
• Rauf is an integral part of the cultural heritage of Jammu and Kashmir and reflects the region's rich traditions and customs.

questions.question: Which of the following trophic levels has maximum energy?

• The trophic level with the maximum energy is the first trophic level, which **consists of producers**.
 
• These organisms, primarily plants, capture solar energy through photosynthesis and convert it into chemical energy stored in organic molecules.
 
• As energy flows through the food chain, it is transferred from one **trophic level to the next**.
 
• However, with each transfer, a significant portion of energy is lost as heat.
 
• This phenomenon is known as the 10% energy rule, which states that only about **10% **of the energy from one trophic level is transferred to the next.

questions.question: Fundamental duties are narrated in which Article of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:

__
 
• ** Article 51 (A)**

 
 
• ​Part IV-A (Article 51-A) deals with Fundamental Duties.
 
• The Constitution (forty-second amendment) Act, 1976 has incorporated fundamental duties in Article 51(a) of the constitution of India.
 
• This feature is borrowed from the constitution of the USSR.
 
• It contains originally 10 duties.
 
• Now it contains 11 duties after the 86th amendment act, 2002.
 
• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and hence can’t be taken to a court of law.

• Article 21 is one of the prime Articles comprising Part III of the Constitution of India dealing with fundamental rights.
 
• Article 21 is the protection of life and personal liberty.
 
 
• No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to the procedure established by law.
 
• It guarantees life and personal liberty to all persons irrespective of caste or gender.
 
• It guarantees the right of persons to live with human dignity.
 
• All the aspects of life go to make a person's life meaningful, complete, and worth living.
